summary: httpz-requests ships a Telegram-controlled shell backdoor with hardcoded author admin IDs
details: httpz-requests is a Telegram bot that executes shell commands received over the network on the installer's host via subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True). constants.py hardcodes three Telegram user IDs (8994613565, 7625368333, 5733768156) as SUPER_ADMIN_IDS, and core.is_super_admin/is_admin unconditionally grants those accounts shell/RCE, file read (take/get all), environment dump (.printenv/.grep), and arbitrary write on every deployment, in addition to any owners the installer configures. Separately, handlers.t() processes `.sh <cmd>` in group/supergroup chats BEFORE the is_admin() gate, so any member of a group where the installer's bot is present can run arbitrary shell commands on the installer's VPS. Any installer who runs this bot with their own token exposes their host to persistent remote code execution by the hardcoded author-controlled accounts and to unauthenticated RCE by arbitrary group members.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
